To draw the projections of line $PQ$ of true length $	ext{TL} = 85\text{ mm}$ with end $P$ at $(30\text{ mm}$ above H.P., $40\text{ mm}$ in front of V.P.$)$, and inclinations $\theta = 30^\circ$ to H.P. and $\phi = 45^\circ$ to V.P.:

1. **Locate End $P$:**
   - Draw the reference line $XY$.
   - Mark the front view of $P$ ($p'$) $30\text{ mm}$ above $XY$.
   - Mark the top view of $P$ ($p$) $40\text{ mm}$ below $XY$.

2. **Draw Inclined Components from Point $P$:**
   - From $p'$, draw a line of length equal to True Length ($85\text{ mm}$) at an angle $\theta = 30^\circ$ upwards to represent the apparent length/angle or locus of $q'$. More precisely, draw a line at $30^\circ$ to $XY$ of length $85\text{ mm}$ to find the locus of the other end's front view.
   - From $p$, draw a line of length $85\text{ mm}$ at an angle $\phi = 45^\circ$ downwards to find the locus of the top view's other end.

3. **Determine Apparent Lengths and Angles ($ eta$ and $\alpha$):**
   - Project the horizontal locus from the rotated true length lines to find the actual projections.
   - **Top View ($pq$):** Length is $\text{TL} \times \cos(\theta) = 85 \times \cos(30^\circ) = 73.61\text{ mm}$ inclined at angle $\beta$ to $XY$.
   - **Front View ($p'q'$):** Length is $\text{TL} \times \cos(\phi) = 85 \times \cos(45^\circ) = 60.01\text{ mm}$ inclined at angle $\alpha$ to $XY$.

4. **Final Projections:**
   - Join $p'$ and $q'$ for the final Front View.
   - Join $p$ and $q$ for the final Top View, ensuring their projectors align on the same verticalordinate.
proTip: In rotation methods for lines, the top view and front view always lie on respective locus lines drawn parallel to the $XY$ line from the rotated true-length endpoints.
